transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I came in because I know this is going to sound kind of hard to explain, but I’ve been really convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are sort of… quietly coordinating opportunities for me.

Like, certain things people say in class, or messages in Slack, they don’t feel random. They feel like coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. And I know that sounds strange, but it’s been hard to shake.
How long have you been feeling like you're receiving these coded signals?

Um… I think about two months? It kind of started when I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program, while I was still doing my operations job, so everything was already kind of overlapping. I remember thinking at first it was just networking stuff, like people being strategic, but then the patterns started feeling more… intentional.
Have you ever heard any voices or sounds that other people cannot hear?

Yeah… I mean, not like a full conversation exactly. But a few times a week, especially when I’m up late working on school stuff or operations plans, I’ll hear my name really clearly, or like a short phrase—once it was “go now”—and I’ll actually check my phone or look around the room.

It’s weird because sometimes I’m already deep in spreadsheets or making a timeline, and I’m thinking about deadlines and who said what in class, and then it’s just… there. But no one’s around when I check.
Do you find it hard to express your thoughts or keep track of what you're saying when you're talking to someone?

Yeah, sometimes. It’s not that I can’t talk, exactly, it’s more like my brain is moving faster than my mouth.

I’ll start explaining one idea, like market expansion for work, and then suddenly I’m thinking about coursework, and then org charts, and then whether moving abroad would make more sense, and I’ll have like five documents open trying to catch all of it. Then I forget which point I was even trying to make first.

So when I’m talking to someone, I can kind of jump around. I know I do it, but in the moment it feels like all the pieces are connected.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized or difficult to follow when you're not trying to explain them to someone?

Yeah… even when I’m not saying it out loud, it’s like everything is sprinting. I’ll be thinking about market expansion, then coursework, then org charts, then like—whether moving abroad would actually be the smarter long-term move, and then I open one document for that, another for a timeline, another for notes…

And then I’ll look at the screen and realize I have five things open and I don’t remember which idea I was originally trying to catch. It all feels connected in my head, but it’s hard to hold onto one thread.
Are these racing thoughts and disorganized ideas causing problems for you at work or in your personal life?

Yeah… it is starting to cause problems. I mean, I’m still showing up, I’m not just disappearing or anything, but my manager has started writing things down—missed handoffs, stuff I said I’d follow up on and then didn’t, or I followed up but in a weird order because I was already onto the next three things.

And school too. On a group assignment, my professor kind of pulled me aside and questioned my judgment, which felt awful because I thought I was seeing the bigger picture. I was trying to connect everything, like roles and deadlines and the final presentation, but I guess it came off as scattered.

So… yeah. It’s straining things with people at work and school enough that I figured I needed to get help before it gets worse.
When you have these racing thoughts, do you feel like they are your own thoughts or do they feel like they are coming from somewhere else?

They feel like mine, I think. It’s not like a voice from somewhere else or anything. It’s more like my own thoughts are just moving too fast and jumping around.

Like I’ll go from market expansion to coursework to org charts to whether moving abroad would be a good idea, and then suddenly I’ve opened five documents trying to catch all of it, and I forget which idea I was even trying to write down first. It feels like me, just… too much of me at once, if that makes sense.
Have you been having difficulty taking care of your daily responsibilities or maintaining your personal appearance?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still showering and getting dressed and showing up places, so it’s not like I’ve completely stopped taking care of myself. But the responsibility side is getting messy.

At work, my manager has started actually documenting things—missed handoffs, things I said I’d follow through on and then didn’t, or I did them out of order. And school has been similar… my professor questioned my judgment on a group project, which really threw me, because I thought I was helping connect everything.

So daily appearance, not really the biggest issue, but keeping up with work and school responsibilities… yeah, that’s been harder, and it’s starting to strain relationships enough that I felt like I needed help.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy or irritable and had a lot of energy?

Yeah… I think so. Most days lately I’ve felt really switched on, like unusually optimistic, like I’m right on the edge of something really big happening. Not just in a normal good-mood way, more like everything is lining up and I can see it before other people do.

But then I also get irritated really fast. Like if a teammate is slow getting back to me, or my boyfriend takes too long to answer something simple, I’ll snap, and afterward I’m like… why did that bother me so much? Normally I don’t think I’d react that strongly. It’s just this mix of feeling energized and excited, but also like everyone else is moving too slowly.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't need much sleep, yet you still had a lot of energy?

I’m not totally sure how to judge that. I mean, I’ve had nights where I stayed up too late because I was thinking about things or trying to finish something, but I don’t know if that counts as “not needing” sleep.

Sometimes I tell myself I’m fine the next day, but then I’ll also drink a lot of coffee, and my schedule is kind of all over the place anyway. Like with work and school, it’s hard to tell what’s energy and what’s just adrenaline or pressure. So… maybe? But I haven’t really tracked it closely.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely happy or irritable that lasted for several days or longer?

Yeah, I think so… like, it hasn’t just been a random good day. It’s been most days where I feel really switched on, almost like I’m on the edge of something huge happening, like I can see connections other people are missing.

But then it flips into irritation really easily. Like if someone on my team takes too long to respond, or my boyfriend doesn’t answer something quickly, I’ll snap over it. And normally that kind of thing wouldn’t bother me that much. So… yeah, it’s lasted beyond just a day or two.
Have you noticed your mood swings affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Yeah… mostly with my boyfriend, and sometimes people I work with who are also kind of friends. I’ll feel really upbeat and like everything is finally clicking, and then if someone takes too long to answer me, I get weirdly irritated and snap.

It’s embarrassing because normally I don’t think a slow text or a teammate being delayed would bother me that much. And then I’ll spend like twenty minutes thinking about how maybe they’re not understanding the importance of what I’m trying to do—sorry, that sounds dramatic. But yeah, it has caused tension. My boyfriend especially notices when I go from really optimistic and intense to annoyed over something small.
Have you been feeling like you have special powers or abilities that others don't have?

Not like… powers, exactly. I don’t think I can fly or anything like that. But I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain—I’ve been really convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are sort of quietly coordinating opportunities for me.

Like, certain comments in class, or little Slack messages, they feel coded… like signals about where my career is supposed to go. And I know if I say it out loud it sounds kind of intense, but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like they’re seeing something in me that other people aren’t saying directly.
Do you feel like you're destined for something great or that you have a special role to play in the world?

Yeah… I mean, “destined” sounds a little embarrassing when you say it that way, but it kind of feels like that. Like I’m supposed to do something bigger than just, you know, manage operations and answer emails all day.

I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been really convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like certain things they say in class, or Slack messages that seem normal to other people, feel like coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. Not in a movie way, exactly, but… it feels directed at me.
Do you believe you have a special or unique mission in life?

Yeah… I think that’s kind of what I mean, even if “mission” sounds really grandiose. It’s more like I keep feeling like my career is being… pointed somewhere, like there’s a specific path I’m supposed to notice.

I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, a comment in class or a Slack message will feel coded, like it’s not just casual—it’s a signal about where I’m supposed to go next.

And I know people network all the time, especially in business school, so it’s not that unusual, but this feels more specific to me. Like they see this role I’m meant to step into before I fully do.
Do you think your mood swings are triggered by something specific happening around you, or do they seem to come out of nowhere?

I don’t know if it’s one specific trigger exactly. Most days lately I’ve just felt really… switched on, like unusually optimistic, like I’m right on the edge of something huge happening.

But then little things around me can set me off. Like if a teammate takes too long to respond, or my boyfriend is moving too slowly when we’re trying to get somewhere, I’ll snap at them, and normally that wouldn’t bother me that much. Then afterward I’m like, why did I react that strongly?

It’s not always out of nowhere, but it’s also not like the situation is big enough to explain it.
Have you recently felt like you can accomplish more than usual in less time, without getting tired?

Yeah, definitely. It’s like I’ve had this constant motor running in me lately. I’ll jump from work dashboards to class readings to organizing volleyball stuff, and I don’t really want to pause.

And it’s funny, because I used to think meetings were just boring—like normal boring—but now sitting through a regular meeting feels almost physically uncomfortable. Like I’m wasting time when I could be doing five other things. I keep thinking, if everyone would just move faster, I could get so much more done.
Do you think you're more intelligent or capable than others?

I don’t know if I’d say “more intelligent” exactly. I mean, I did well in school and I can usually keep up, but that’s not really the thing.

It’s more like… sometimes I feel like I’m seeing connections faster than other people, or like I’m three steps ahead in a discussion and everyone else is still debating the obvious part. But then I also don’t want to sound arrogant, because there are plenty of people in my program who are really smart.

Sorry, that probably didn’t answer it cleanly. I guess I feel more capable lately, but I’m not sure if that means I think I’m better than people.
Have you recently felt invincible or like you're not bound by the same rules as other people?

Invincible? I don’t know… that feels like a big word. I wouldn’t say I think rules don’t apply to me exactly.

I mean, sometimes I get impatient with how things are supposed to be done, like paperwork or waiting for approvals or people making everything into a process. At work there are all these little steps for things, and half of them feel like they were designed by someone who never actually has to get anything done, you know? Sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

But no, I don’t think I’m above everyone or anything. I just… maybe I feel more confident than usual, but not invincible.
Do you think your feelings of being destined for something great or having a special role are related to your overall mood and energy levels?

Yeah… I think they probably are connected, because before this whole stretch of feeling so keyed up and driven, that wasn’t really happening.

Like, before I started the MBA prereqs and my workload got so intense, I wasn’t sitting there thinking things had hidden meanings or that messages were, I don’t know, coded for me. And I definitely wasn’t hearing my name when nobody was actually there. That all kind of started after my mood and energy shifted.

I mean, I’ve always been busy—work gets hectic, volleyball stuff, school plans, all of that—but this feels different from just being motivated. So… yes, I think it lines up with the energy thing.

Yeah… I think that’s kind of what I mean, even if “mission” sounds really grandiose. It’s more like I keep feeling like my career is being… pointed somewhere, like there’s a specific path I’m supposed to notice.

I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like, a comment in class or a Slack message will feel coded, like it’s not just casual—it’s a signal about where I’m supposed to go next.

And I know people network all the time, especially in business school, so it’s not that unusual, but this feels more specific to me. Like they see this role I’m meant to step into before I fully do.

I don’t know if it’s one specific trigger exactly. Most days lately I’ve just felt really… switched on, like unusually optimistic, like I’m right on the edge of something huge happening.

But then little things around me can set me off. Like if a teammate takes too long to respond, or my boyfriend is moving too slowly when we’re trying to get somewhere, I’ll snap at them, and normally that wouldn’t bother me that much. Then afterward I’m like, why did I react that strongly?

It’s not always out of nowhere, but it’s also not like the situation is big enough to explain it.

Yeah, definitely. It’s like I’ve had this constant motor running in me lately. I’ll jump from work dashboards to class readings to organizing volleyball stuff, and I don’t really want to pause.

And it’s funny, because I used to think meetings were just boring—like normal boring—but now sitting through a regular meeting feels almost physically uncomfortable. Like I’m wasting time when I could be doing five other things. I keep thinking, if everyone would just move faster, I could get so much more done.

I don’t know if I’d say “more intelligent” exactly. I mean, I did well in school and I can usually keep up, but that’s not really the thing.

It’s more like… sometimes I feel like I’m seeing connections faster than other people, or like I’m three steps ahead in a discussion and everyone else is still debating the obvious part. But then I also don’t want to sound arrogant, because there are plenty of people in my program who are really smart.

Sorry, that probably didn’t answer it cleanly. I guess I feel more capable lately, but I’m not sure if that means I think I’m better than people.
